Fix times after midnight written as early morning times

Source: R/fix_overnight_times.R
fix_overnight_times.Rd

Rewrites the times after midnight of trips that run past it, when they are written as early morning times (e.g. "00:10:00" after "23:50:00"), as times past "24:00:00" (e.g. "24:10:00"), as required by the GTFS specification. All gtfstools functions that calculate or edit durations and speeds or use information on time of day use fix_overnight_times() internally to fix the overnight times.

Usage

fix_overnight_times(gtfs)

Arguments

gtfs

A GTFS object, as created by read_gtfs().

Value

A GTFS object with the time columns of its stop_times and the end_time column of its frequencies fixed.

Details

The arrival and departure times of each trip are read in order of stop_sequence, ignoring blank times. A time more than 12 hours earlier than the previous time of its trip is taken as a time after midnight, so it and the later times of the trip are moved one day later (e.g. "00:10:00" becomes "24:10:00"). Trips that run past a second midnight are moved two days, and so on. A time more than 12 hours later than the previous time of its trip undoes one of these days, so feeds that mix both forms are also fixed (e.g. "24:30:00", "00:40:00", "24:50:00" becomes "24:30:00", "24:40:00", "24:50:00"), and trips whose times already follow the specification are left unchanged. Blank times are kept blank. Only stop_times and frequencies are modified; their existing _secs columns are updated to match.

Times earlier than the previous time of their trip by 12 hours or less are left unchanged, with a warning. Times are never moved earlier, so trips with known times more than 12 hours apart that follow the specification (e.g. "06:00:00", "19:30:00") are left unchanged. Rows with a missing trip_id or stop_sequence are left unchanged, and stops with duplicated stop_sequences are read in the order of their rows (see remove_duplicates()).

Trips whose times are all written after midnight as early morning times (e.g. a trip of the previous service day departing at "00:30:00") can't be told apart from trips of the service day and are left unchanged.

In frequencies, an end_time earlier than the start_time of its row is moved by whole days to the first time later than the start_time (e.g. "23:00:00"-"01:00:00" becomes "23:00:00"-"25:00:00"). A start_time written as an early morning time is left unchanged. The template times of trips listed in frequencies are fixed as any other times, which doesn't change their departures, since only the differences between them are used.

An error is raised if a fixed time would be later than "9999:59:59".

See also

fix_gtfs(), convert_time_to_seconds()

Examples

library(dplyr)

data_path <- system.file("extdata/poa_gtfs.zip", package = "gtfstools")

gtfs <- read_gtfs(data_path)

# this trip runs past midnight, but its last time is written as "00:02:00"
gtfs$stop_times |>
  filter(trip_id == "T2-1@1#2310", arrival_time != "") |>
  select(trip_id, stop_sequence, arrival_time, departure_time)
#>        trip_id stop_sequence arrival_time departure_time
#>         <char>         <int>       <char>         <char>
#> 1: T2-1@1#2310             1     23:10:00       23:10:00
#> 2: T2-1@1#2310            62     00:02:00       00:02:00

fixed_gtfs <- fix_overnight_times(gtfs)

fixed_gtfs$stop_times |>
  filter(trip_id == "T2-1@1#2310", arrival_time != "") |>
  select(trip_id, stop_sequence, arrival_time, departure_time)
#>        trip_id stop_sequence arrival_time departure_time
#>         <char>         <int>       <char>         <char>
#> 1: T2-1@1#2310             1     23:10:00       23:10:00
#> 2: T2-1@1#2310            62     24:02:00       24:02:00
